title: The slot service dropped a held attempt before the capacity was declared again, so a journal failure or a crash between the record's removal and the declaration lost the declaration for good
resolution: Before the reclaim of a held attempt the service owes the declaration in the journal (oweCapacityDeclaration), which every later successful reclaim and every start journal through recordCapacity; slot and start tests with a journal failure and a crash fail before the fix.

title: After a durable reclaimFailed, a fault of the kill, the proof, or the release turned the reclaim into unavailable, so no reclaim-failed line was logged and no later reclaim finished the cleanup
resolution: Every outcome after the durable failure is reclaim-failed; a later reclaim, also after a restart, kills through ReclaimHost.killRecorded on Linux, proves the containment empty, and frees it without the program; tests of the three faults fail before the fix.

title: The three new start failures repeated the raw error message, which can name a checkout path that the credential redaction keeps
resolution: faultMessage gives a fixed message with only a system error code such as EACCES; a test of the line that workerMain writes for the hard-link read, the sweep, and the record read fails before the fix.

title: The adapter's handOffRecords had no direct test: worker tests replaced it with a fake and adapter tests called handedOff
resolution: Adapter tests read real records, also through a reopened adapter, reject a malformed and an unreadable record, and leave out one removed between the listing and its read; they fail against the code before handOffRecords and against mutants of each branch.

title: The scenario Reclaim after the exit refused every offer while a hand-off record existed, which contradicts Slot only on a macOS worker with several slots
resolution: The scenario now holds every slot of the worker, one of them by the handed-off attempt, as the architect's answer N2 keeps held slots counting on macOS.

title: The execution wire contract still declared capacity only at enrollment and on a change, while the worker now declares it again after every reclaim that removes a hand-off record
resolution: The Capacity declared row now also names the declaration after such a reclaim, also unchanged, with a link to Git workspace section 3, step 6; listed under Contract amendments.

title: The contract and the containment requirement still proved every recorded containment without a kill, although a later reclaim of a failed program kills its cgroup first on Linux
resolution: Both now prove without a kill only a record without a failure, and send a record with reclaimFailed to the cleanup of a failed program (Killed reclaim containment).

title: No test checked that the one-account kill spares the group of an exited program, the guard behind the claim that a reused group is never killed
resolution: ProcessGroupReclaimHost takes an injected SendSignal; tests show SIGKILL to the unreaped group only, none for an exited or recorded group; a mutant without the guard fails two of them.

title: A fault of the durable reclaimFailed write returned at once, so a program past its run bound kept running and every later reclaim waited out the proof
resolution: The containment is killed, proven empty, and freed also after that fault, and the write's unavailable is returned; a later reclaim runs the program again; a test with a read-only record directory fails before.

title: The Interrupted cleanup scenario said a later reclaim kills the recorded containment on every platform, and the requirement had lost the sentence that a containment populated at the bound stays
resolution: The scenario kills only the Linux cgroup and on one account only proves the group empty without a signal; the requirement again keeps a containment populated at the bound.

title: The author self-check named Git workspace composition at 463 characters as the longest requirement, which the pass 1 fixes had made stale
resolution: The self-check gives 463 as the figure before the review fixes and points to Independent review for the later lengths.

title: The revision list credited 00a1e2b0 with the spec text of findings 1 to 3, though the git-workspace-port delta of finding 2 is in 004144e1
resolution: The list names 004144e1 for the git-workspace-port delta of finding 2 and 00a1e2b0 for the worker-runtime delta and the contract text.

title: A file system call that threw while the reclaimFailed record was renamed into place skipped the kill, the proof, and the release of an overrunning program
resolution: The write runs through failingFileSystemAsUnavailable, so a thrown fault becomes unavailable and the cleanup still runs, while a simulated crash still rejects; a rename fault test fails before.

title: Concurrent reclaims shared the one owed capacity declaration, so the first reclaim's declaration cleared the debt of the second, also across a crash after the second removal
resolution: WorkspaceSlots runs its reclaims one at a time, so each owes and declares its own; two barrier tests, one with a crash after the second removal, fail before.

title: The scenario Failure record not written said every write fault leaves the record without the failure, though a failed directory flush after the rename leaves reclaimFailed
resolution: The scenario, the contract, the design, and this change's record separate a fault before the rename from one after it; a new scenario and test cover the failed flush after the rename.
